findings.title: All app imports are still started eagerly
findings.body: Each `import()` is evaluated while this object is constructed, so importing the app-store barrel immediately starts loading every app module, even when the caller needs only one. This does not provide on-demand loading and means a cold request that first touches the app store can still pay for loading and evaluating all app packages.

findings.title: Reschedule does not wait for calendar deletion
findings.body: `forEach` discards the promises returned by its async callbacks. Since `getCalendar` now requires an asynchronous import, the callback can still be waiting for the app module when this function finishes sending the email and returns; the old calendar event can therefore remain in place after rescheduling, and callback failures will not be caught by the surrounding `try/catch`. Await the callbacks, for example with `Promise.all`.

findings.title: Reschedule does not wait for calendar deletion
findings.body: `forEach` discards the promises returned by its async callbacks. Since `getCalendar` now requires an asynchronous import, the callback can still be waiting for the app module when this function finishes sending the email and returns; the old calendar event can therefore remain in place after rescheduling, and callback failures will not be caught by the surrounding `try/catch`. Await the callbacks, for example with `Promise.all`.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation can finish before calendar deletions are tracked
findings.body: The async callback is not awaited by `forEach`. It only adds a deletion to `apiDeletes` after awaiting both `getCalendar` and `deleteEvent`, while the outer handler can reach its later `Promise.all` before either finishes. The handler may then delete booking references and report cancellation without deleting the external recurring calendar events; any later callback failure also escapes the surrounding flow.

findings.title: Reschedule does not wait for integration deletions
findings.body: `forEach` discards the promises returned by its async callbacks. The mutation can proceed to send the reschedule email and return while a callback is still awaiting `getCalendar`, leaving the old calendar event undeleted when the request completes. Errors from those callbacks are also not propagated. Await the callbacks, for example with `Promise.all`.
